title: Is the Mean Girls movie musical… actually good? #MeanGirls #MeanGirls...
transcript: I'm a certified Mean Girls, a musical hater, and I went to see the Mean Girls movie because, honestly, I heard it was good, and I wanted to see if this would change my mind. Honestly, I am just as surprised as you are that I actually had a really good time at this movie. Like, I still don't think it's a very good musical, but I do think that the movie improved upon the stage version in almost every conceivable way. For starters, they cut a lot of the songs, and normally in movie musicals, that's a big no no for me. But in this one, it actually worked, because, one, a lot of the songs that they cut just weren't that good. And 2, it helps tremendously with the pacing of the show. And for the songs that we do get, there's actually a tremendous amount of effort into translating those to the screen. Like, the trailers may have been embarrassed that this movie is a musical, but the actual movie itself fully embraces its musical roots. So even for songs that I don't care for as much, like I'd rather be me or Revenge Party, there's so much going on on screen that I am less distracted by how bad the lyrics are. Take I'd rather be me for an example. That song is filmed almost entirely to look like one continuous shot, and we see Janice running through the hallways of the school into various rooms. And it's genuinely impressive what they were able to pull off. And they very easily could have just had Janice standing in the middle of the auditorium singing her power ballad and called it a day. But the fact that they didn't, and what the extra mile, I really appreciate it. And as I reflect on a lot of the things that I did not care for in the stage adaptation, one of the biggest things is that it just felt really lazy to me. Like, the set was mostly projections. The choreography felt like a carbon copy of, like, every other Casey Nicolaugh show. And as an adaptation, it just felt like the movie, but worse. I think that this movie easily could have fallen into the same traps. I mean, it is Mean Girls. It has the name going for it. It doesn't really need to try that hard. Well, yes, not every single choice worked for me. I appreciated that they actually made choices. I also think the attempts to modernize the story worked way better for me on film than they did on stage. Especially the way that they incorporated social media, which I think when done poorly, can feel really, really forced and out of touch. But here actually worked really well. I want to shout out the cast as well, who are really great across the board and I think do a really good job and making these roles their own and not just Imitating the original movie, I do think that Katie's voice is just F. But honestly it didn't bother me as much as I thought it would. And obviously Joe Paul Spivey, Ali Carvallo, and Rene Rapp are carrying this film on their backs and vocally incredible. And so yeah, against all odds, I actually really enjoyed the Mean Girls movie. If I had to give it a star rating, I would probably give it a 3.5 out of 5 stars, because it's definitely not the greatest movie ever made, but it's pretty good and I actually had a really good time.
